'''Catherine Drew Harvell''' is an American-born marine ecologist who researches ocean biodiversity and ocean health, specializing in diseases in marine ecosystems.

== Early life and education ==
Harvell was born in Boston, Massachusetts, United States.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|last=Harvell|first=Catherine Drew|title=The larval behavior, life history traits, and adaptations to predation and competition of Dendrobeania lichenoides (Bryozoa, Cheilostomata)|work=Masters Thesis|publisher=University of Alberta|year=1981|isbn=978-0-315-06014-2|location=ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Publishing, ProQuest Document ID 303210700}}</ref> Harvell completed her bachelor's degree in zoology with honors from the [[University of Alberta]] in 1978. She remained at University of Alberta to complete a master's degree in zoology, supervised by Fu-Shiang Chia. She completed her thesis and graduated in 1981.<ref name=":2" /> She attended the [[University of Washington]] to complete a Ph.D. in zoology and graduated in 1985.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Harvell|first=C. Drew|title=Partial predation, inducible defenses, and the population biology of a marine bryozoan (Membranipora membranacea)|year=1985|oclc=13024784}}</ref>

== Research career ==
In 1986, Harvell joined the faculty in the Department of Ecology & Evolutionary Biology at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Saulnier|first=Beth|date=2019|title=A Sea of Troubles|url=http://cornellalumnimagazine.com/a-sea-of-troubles/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Cornell Alumni Magazine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190717135200/http://cornellalumnimagazine.com:80/a-sea-of-troubles/ |archive-date=2019-07-17 }}</ref> Her research group focuses on a range of topics, including marine invertebrate biology and diversity to climate change and its impacts on [[disease ecology]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Katie |last2=Ahearn |first2=Ashley |date=2014-06-29 |title=Infectious disease cited in die-off |pages=A6 |work=Statesman Journal |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/115528351/infectious-disease-cited-in-die-off/ |access-date=2022-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Yong |first=Ed |date=2019-01-30 |title=A Starfish-Killing Disease Is Remaking the Oceans |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2019/01/starfish-killing-disease-remaking-oceans/581632/ |access-date=2022-12-31 |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref>

In 1998 Harvell co-edited a book with Ralph Tollrian on ''The Ecology and Evolution of Inducible Defenses''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The ecology and evolution of inducible defenses|date=1999|publisher=Princeton University Press|others=Ralph Tollrian, C. Drew Harvell|isbn=0-691-01221-0|location=Princeton, N.J.|oclc=38890836}}</ref> In 2016, Harvell published her first book for the popular media, ''A Sea of Glass: Searching for the Blaschkas' Fragile Legacy in an Ocean at Risk''.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q114635674|mode=cs1 <!-- A Sea of Glass: Searching for the Blaschkas’ Fragile Legacy in an Ocean at Risk --> |author-last=Harvell |author-first=Drew |author-link=Drew Harvell |series=Organisms and Environments, 13. |edition=1st, hardcover |isbn=978-0-520-28568-2 }}<!-- Please use Q114634846 if needed to cite the work itself, instead of the publication. --></ref> The book explores Harvell's work as curator of the Cornell University Collection of [[Blaschka invertebrate models|Blaschka Invertebrate Models]], which includes 570 detailed and highly accurate sculptures of marine creatures.<ref name=":0" /> Her second book in the popular press was published in 2019, titled ''Ocean Outbreak: Confronting the Rising Tide of Marine Disease''.<ref name=":1" /> This book explores how corals, abalone, salmon, and starfish are being impacted by outbreaks of infectious diseases and suggestions actions that can be taken.

She wrote [[The Ocean's Menagerie]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gee |first=Henry |date=2025-04-18 |title=A deep dive into the strange kingdom of the ocean |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/ocean-menagerie-earth-strangest-creatures-reshape-rules-life-drew-harvell-review-djxb6r0v9 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Harvell's recognitions for her writing and professional accomplishments include:

2015 - Elected to the [[Ecological Society of America]] (ESA) Fellows Program<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mize|first=Alison|date=May 7, 2015|title=Ecological Society of America announces 2015 fellows|url=https://www.esa.org/blog/2015/05/07/ecological-society-of-america-announces-2015-fellows/|url-status=live|access-date=2020-06-08|website=ESA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505220310/https://www.esa.org/blog/2015/05/07/ecological-society-of-america-announces-2015-fellows/ |archive-date=2019-05-05 }}</ref>

2016 - [[National Outdoor Book Award]] Winner, in the category of Natural History Literature for ''A Sea of Glass: Searching for the Blaschkas’ Fragile Legacy in an Ocean at Risk''.<ref>{{Cite web|last=National Outdoor Book Awards Foundation|title=Winners of the 2016 National Outdoor Book Awards|url=http://www.noba-web.org/books16.htm|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-08|website=National Outdoor Book Awards|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170122041944/http://www.noba-web.org:80/books16.htm |archive-date=2017-01-22 }}</ref>

2016 - The Best “Art Meets Science” Books of 2016, one of eight books named by ''[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian Magazine]]'', for ''A Sea of Glass: Searching for the Blaschkas’ Fragile Legacy in an Ocean at Risk''.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Fessenden|first=Marissa|date=December 2, 2016|title=The Best "Art Meets Science" Books of 2016|url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/best-art-meets-science-books-2016-180961237/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-09|website=Smithsonian Magazine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203155347/http://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/best-art-meets-science-books-2016-180961237/ |archive-date=2016-12-03 }}</ref>

2017 - Honorable Mention, Rachel Carson Environment Book Award, [[Society of Environmental Journalists]], for ''A Sea of Glass: Searching for the Blaschkas’ Fragile Legacy in an Ocean at Risk.''<ref>{{Cite web|last=The Society of Environmental Journalists|date=2017|title=Winners: SEJ 16th Annual Awards for Reporting on the Environment|url=https://www.sej.org/winners-sej-16th-annual-awards-reporting-environment|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Society of Environmental Journalists|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815235213/http://www.sej.org/winners-sej-16th-annual-awards-reporting-environment |archive-date=2017-08-15 }}</ref>

2020 - [[Ecological Society of America]] (ESA) [[Sustainability science|Sustainability Science]] Award, which recognizes the authors of the scholarly work that makes the greatest contribution to the emerging science of ecosystem and regional sustainability through the integration of ecological and social sciences.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2021|title=ESA Announces 2020 Award Recipients and 2019 Student Awards|journal=The Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America|language=en|volume=102|issue=1|pages=e01790|doi=10.1002/bes2.1790|issn=2327-6096|doi-access=free|bibcode=2021BuESA.102E1790. }}</ref>

2020 - [[PROSE Awards|PROSE Award]] for Biological Sciences, for ''Ocean Outbreak: Confronting the Rising Tide of Marine Disease''.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Association of American Publishers (AAP)|date=2020|title=2020 Winners|url=https://proseawards.com/winners/2020-award-winners/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Winners|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427095343/https://proseawards.com/winners/2020-award-winners/ |archive-date=2020-04-27 }}</ref>

2020 - Selected to give the Rachel Carson Lecture for the [[American Geophysical Union]] (AGU) Fall Meeting 2020 on "Oceanic Pandemics from Foundation to [[Keystone species|Keystone Species]]."<ref>{{Citation|title=Oceanic Pandemics from Foundation to Keystone Species| bibcode=2020AGUFMOS027..01H |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Og8YLynyKM|language=en|access-date=2021-06-08 | last1=Harvell | first1=D. | journal=AGU Fall Meeting Abstracts | year=2020 | volume=2020 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Harvell is married with a daughter and a son who is a writer.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Harvell|first=C. Drew|title=Ocean outbreak : confronting the rising tide of marine disease|date=2019|isbn=978-0-520-29697-8|location=Oakland, California|oclc=1055264300}}</ref>
